elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted subparagraph: "In addition to Subparagraph 18.1, Teleglobe USA Inc. may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, whether during or after the Initial Period...". In this consortium structure "terminate its participation" is the same exit construct used by 18.1 for a Party's departure, so it is the functional equivalent of Customer termination of the Agreement. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" fails only mechanically, because the right is granted to the named entity "Teleglobe USA Inc." rather than to a generic alias (Customer/Client/etc.); the drafter should confirm on the signature/parties page that Teleglobe USA Inc. is our client, since nothing in the cited text establishes that.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties" — 30 days, in writing, and no additional condition or consent requirement is attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "the other Parties shall refund to Teleglobe USA Inc., pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination" — express "pro rata", express post-effective-date period, and the payer obligation runs against the counterparties.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained 18.1/18.2: a Party may unilaterally "terminate its participation ... at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter", and during the Initial Period the Agreement may be terminated only "by agreement in writing of all the Parties". The new right is drafted as Teleglobe-only, so it does not create a mid-term convenience exit for the other Parties.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (it is better than fallback and satisfies the preferred element instead).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee attaches to the new right. The only exit penalty in Paragraph 18 is the capital-cost forfeiture, which by its terms applies only to "a Party that terminates its participation in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1", and the new right is expressly "[i]n addition to Subparagraph 18.1".

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 permits unilateral Party termination only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; mid-term termination requires unanimous written agreement under 18.2.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice", which exceeds 90 days.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single inserted subparagraph supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice and the express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts, and the counterparty-side element was already satisfied by retained 18.1/18.2 (no unilateral mid-Initial-Period exit).
Fallback is not complete (30 days sits outside the 60–90 day band), but that does not matter because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimal: one concise insertion, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or damages add-ons, and no disturbance of the 18.4 capital-cost forfeiture or the 18.7 continuing-liability mechanic, both of which remain tied to Subparagraph 18.1.

Intent preserved: 18.1's end-of-Initial-Period exit, the 18.2 unanimity route, the Management Committee 90% mechanic and the 18.7 liability apportionment all survive without contradiction, and the new right is expressly additive ("In addition to Subparagraph 18.1").

Drafting points to tidy without changing substance: (a) confirm on the parties page that Teleglobe USA Inc. is our client — the deterministic alias check failed because the right is granted to a named entity rather than a playbook alias; (b) give the new text a subparagraph number (e.g. 18.8) so it is citable and does not read as a continuation of 18.7; (c) consider whether "any amounts prepaid by it" should be tied to prepaid charges/contributions for the post-termination period, since the other Parties may argue it sweeps in capital contributions and circumvents the 18.4 no-credit rule; (d) the Agreement contains no asset-realization/interest-reallocation mechanic for a mid-Initial-Period withdrawal, so expect the counterparties to ask for one — that is a negotiation exposure, not an element defect.
